schemaNote: Regional index for GPIR Americas. Americas is a BROADER REGIONAL INDEX, not a second country database: any country already covered under LATAM (assets/data/latam-countries.json) keeps LATAM as its ONE canonical intelligence record and is intentionally NOT listed again here — that would read as a duplicate country even though no data was actually duplicated, so this file only carries the countries Americas genuinely owns. The 'latamCoverage' field on each sub-region documents which LATAM countries fall geographically within it, purely so the directory page can link out to LATAM instead of silently omitting the topic. Countries listed below (canonicalRegion 'americas') have no equivalent LATAM record: Canada, United States, ten Anglophone/Dutch-speaking sovereign Caribbean states, Guyana and Suriname. 'status' follows the same convention used across APAC/LATAM/Europe: active = a real, published Country Intelligence page exists; coming_soon = the country is on the GPIR roadmap but no page is published yet. No country in this release is active — Americas launches honestly, the same way LATAM did, with real classification and currency data but no fabricated intelligence content.
regionDescriptor: Northern America, Central America, the Caribbean and South America — cross-border payments, instant payment systems, banking infrastructure, fintech ecosystems and regulatory developments across the Americas.
regionalFrameworkNote: Sub-region groupings follow the UN M49 geographic classification (Northern America, Central America, Caribbean, South America) for navigation purposes only. This does not imply that countries within a grouping share identical payment systems, economic structures or regulatory regimes.

territoriesNote: Caribbean territories, dependencies and special markets (e.g. Puerto Rico, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Aruba, Curaçao, British Virgin Islands, Turks and Caicos Islands, US Virgin Islands, Montserrat, Anguilla) are intentionally excluded from the sovereign-country count above and are not represented as countries. GPIR intends a separate 'Caribbean Territories / Special Markets' structure for these in a future sprint, classified explicitly as TERRITORY, SPECIAL MARKET or DEPENDENCY rather than as sovereign states.
